title: SDK contracts: experimental cursors, reroute fallbacks, and rollout PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines a minimal, backwards-compatible contract across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs for resumable streaming and cursor-based pagination, plus a network-failure reroute/fallback policy. Goal: ship an interoperable, low-risk rollout that lets hosted and dedicated customers adopt resumable streams without breaking existing pagination or retry semantics.

Background & motivation:
Teams building conversational or streaming features need a reproducible way to resume partially consumed responses (e.g., client reconnects, mobile backgrounding). Current SDKs expose incompatible resume semantics across languages, and some clients degrade to full re-fetch which increases cost and can return inconsistent outputs. We must standardize an opaque cursor token format, retry/backoff behavior, and a server-side reroute policy (when model variant changes or capacity shifts) so clients can gracefully continue or fallback to polling.

Scope (in):
- Define cursor token shape (opaque base64 blob with version header) and lifetime expectations.
- SDK surface: resume_stream(cursor) API, stream iterator with explicit checkpoints, and a paginated list iterator that can accept a resume token.
- Cross-language examples for Python, TS, and Go with consistent semantics.
- Retry policy defaults: idempotent-safe retries for streaming frames, exponential backoff with jitter, and a thin hook for client overrides.
- Fallback behavior: automatic reroute to a compatible model variant + explicit client callback when content may have changed.
- Acceptance criteria & test vectors for interop testing.

Scope (out):
- Major API redesign of existing SDKs (we will add surface but keep legacy methods).
- New server-side caching layer changes unrelated to resume format (we will document expectations but not implement here).

Design decisions and rationale:
- Opaque token: clients must not parse token contents. Version header allows future migration. Rationale: prevents brittle client logic and permits server host to change underlying routing.
- Resume semantics: resume is eventually consistent. If server reroutes to a different model variant, we must surface a metadata flag (server_changed=true) so UIs can decide to re-render or mark content as potentially altered. Rationale: avoids silent semantic shifts.
- Idempotency and retries: streaming frames are sequence-numbered; clients retry by requesting from last confirmed sequence. Non-idempotent server-side side-effects are out-of-scope.

API surface (examples):
- Python: Client.stream_conversation(prompt, checkpoint_every=64) -> yields Frame objects; Frame.checkpoint() -> returns resume_token; Client.resume_stream(resume_token) -> yields remaining frames.
- TypeScript: client.streamConversation(prompt, {checkpointEvery: 64}) returns AsyncIterable<Frame>; frame.checkpoint(): string; client.resumeStream(token: string): AsyncIterable<Frame>.
- Go: StreamConversation(ctx, prompt, opts) returns chan Frame and ResumeToken type string.

Rollout plan and compatibility strategy:
1) Spec & SDK stubs (this ticket): implement new APIs in parallel to existing methods and add deprecation notes.
2) Internal dogfooding: runtime and console teams to adopt for selected beta customers (~2 weeks).
3) Public beta: opt-in flag in hosted API and SDK. Collect telemetry on resume success rates and reroutes.
4) Gradual enforcement: after 8 weeks, recommend replacement in docs; deprecation window of 6 months for legacy-only usage.

Testing and interop validation:
- Provide canonical test vectors: short stream, mid-stream reconnect, forced reroute response.
- Cross-language runner to verify that resume_token produced by one SDK can resume in another.
- Chaos tests: simulate network partitions and server-side reroutes.

Monitoring & observability:
- Add telemetry events: resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_failure_reason, reroute_occurred.
- Console dashboard: per-model resume success percentage and average resumption latency.

Acceptance criteria (see list below for machine-checkable items).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: clients misuse opaque token (attempt to inspect). Mitigation: SDKs will throw on parse attempts and docs will emphasize opacity.
- Risk: reroute leads to content drift and customer-confusion. Mitigation: server_changed flag + UI guidance and canary rollouts.

Open questions for follow-ups:
- TTL for resume tokens (recommend 24 hours but need infra confirmation).
- How to represent partial tokens for extremely long streams? (stream checkpoint chunking).
- Back-compat policy for legacy SDKs that will never implement resume.
acceptance_criteria: Opaque resume_token format versioned and documented; SDKs accept and return tokens as strings
Cross-language interop: token produced by Python SDK resumes correctly using TS and Go SDKs (interop test pass)
Resume attempt success rate >= 99% in controlled internal dogfood for short/mid-length streams
Reroute events surface server_changed=true in resume metadata and are logged in telemetry
SDKs expose default retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter; allow override via client options
No breaking changes to existing simple non-resumable streaming APIs; legacy methods remain supported
Automated tests covering reconnect, partial checkpoint, and server-induced reroute are added to CI
Console shows resume_success_rate metric and alert when it drops below 95% for any model variant
